title: Minimum Operations for 90-Degree Rotational Symmetry
description:
You are given an `n x n` integer matrix `grid`. In one operation, you may choose any cell `(r, c)` and either increment `grid[r][c]` by `1` or decrement `grid[r][c]` by `1`.

Return the **minimum total number of operations** required so that `grid` becomes identical to its own `90`-degree clockwise rotation (i.e., `grid[r][c] == grid[c][n - 1 - r]` for all `0 <= r, c < n`).
hints: Under 90-degree clockwise rotation, the matrix splits into disjoint 4-cell orbits {(r, c), (c, n-1-r), (n-1-r, n-1-c), (n-1-c, r)}, plus an invariant center cell when n is odd.
All four values in an orbit must be made equal; for sorted values a <= b <= c <= d, the minimum L1 cost is achieved at any target in [b, c] and equals (d - a) + (c - b).

examples.explanation: All four cells form one orbit [1, 2, 3, 4]; bringing them to 2 or 3 costs (4 - 1) + (3 - 2) = 4.
The matrix is already invariant under 90-degree clockwise rotation, requiring 0 operations.
Corner orbit [1, 5, 1, 5] costs 8, edge orbit [2, 2, 6, 2] costs 4, and the center cell 9 is invariant, totaling 12.
